items.title: Fix Desk Issues

Levant: Levant: I read the Desk face and the desk server's publish path. I did not run the desk, so the G23.2 cause is not confirmed.

- **Subscriptions exist per element.** The List subscribes at `desk.js:1711`, the dialog at `deskDetails.js:620`, Team at `desk.js:898`, and deskVerify at `desk.js:1722`. Each calls its own `onPublished`.
- **Dialog wrong-item risk.** `deskDetails.js` keeps one set of module globals (`ddId`, `ddFacts`). `open()` sets `ddId`, `ddTake` drops any change not for `ddId`, and `ddPress` reads `ddId` at click time. A press can only reach the wrong item if two dialog instances share those globals while the older one is still on screen. I have not read how the shell's `callDialog` reuses or stacks instances, so that is the next thing to check.
- **List additions pull.** `deskOnPublished` (`desk.js:515-523`) inserts nothing for an unknown item. It calls `deskSearchItems()`, which asks the server again. That is a pull, against "no pulling", and it is what the "List takes additions" topic should replace: insert the row the publish carries, at the position the server gives.

items.title: deskUnsloth: tool lists follow more
items.box:
deskUnsloth gets a family's verbs in full, in two steps: first the list of verbs, then the details of each verb it keeps.
AGENTS.introspect answers the verbs' names only, not their descriptions, so a family's whole list fits one answer; each verb's description and request come from AGENTS.<verb>, one ask per verb, as deskUnsloth already reads them.
deskUnsloth may withhold verbs from Levant after reading the list; it asks details only of the verbs it keeps.
A listing that still says more is a loud failure in the suites, never a silent loss of tools; there is no paging.
introSpector.js is common code serving the node's namespaces too; the change is to what introspect's labels carry, its request and reply shape stay.
Test: a family whose descriptions together pass one answer is listed whole by name, and every verb's details reach Levant's tools; a census suite fails when any family's listing says more.

Levant: Here's the run on **goal/G24.9**, in order.

**The ask.** Andy opened the item — "Andy can delete an item that no longer serves him from its item details, without switching the goal into design mode" — and asked Levant to fill the box: what it would take to let the user delete items.

**Levant's box v1.** Delete offered on any item that is not a goal, whatever the goal's design mode, except while an agent holds a phase on it (red/build/verify), and except on an item claimed done and not yet closed. The button and the verb share one rule — `buttons()` in desk.js offers delete, and `item.delete` is refused exactly when the button is not. Erases nothing, per the G9.7 ruling: the item is closed, left out, keeps its box/checks/chat, blocks nothing, still found by Include Closed. The armed Delete→Delete: sure? button already existed; only the server rule changed.

**The review (claude-windows).** Checked every citation against the code — design-mode rule at desk.js:1206, `item.delete` closing and leaving out at :929, the verb refused by the same rule, G9.7 quoted right. All held. Noted the button already exists (deskDetails.js:158–163), so the only build was the server rule in `buttons()`; flagged one open question: should Delete be offered on a phase-held item or a done item?

**The cap (Andy).** "No. If a phase is held, no delete." So Delete is offered only on items with no phase held.

**The red Q.** The item had no checks on it, so a blocking red Q (check.add, kind Q) was placed on the one point the box didn't rule — delete on a done item.

**The answer (Andy).** "No" — Delete is not offered on an item claimed done and not yet closed.

**Q1 passed.** Box v2 recorded the ruling: no Delete on a done item; yes on items with no phase held.

Net: the rule is now fully decided — Delete offered on any non-goal item with no phase held, refused on a held phase and on a done-but-not-closed item, never on a goal, and it erases nothing. The only remaining build was `buttons()` sharing one rule with `item.delete`, which claude-windows had already confirmed against the code.
